Goals.Goal: **The shape schema (`F207`), declared and enforced.** A single declared schema for the seven record files and the seven golden fixtures: per file, the expected root element and the root attribute set (`base`, `headroom`, `ceiling`, present on live roots and absent on retired siblings); the one genre element tag; the genre element's required attribute set and value forms (`id` lower-kebab with dot-slugs, `token` upper `F`/`D` with dot-slugs, `status` agreeing with the holding file; `Row.name` a `C-*` name, `Row.kind` in `chartered` / `sweep-remainder` / `historical`; `Entry.genre` in `finding` / `decision`, `Entry.layer` in `live` / `retired`); the required children and their order (`Finding`: `PaidBy`? `Title` `Body`; `Decision`: `Title` `Body` (`CodifiedIn` | `TaughtIn`)*; `Row`: `Number` `Charter` `Pays` `StatusText` `Successor`?; `Entry`: none, self-closing); the optional children; and the depth bound (genre elements only as direct children of the root, leaves only as their children). The schema is the **engine's contract, not a snapshot of the corpus**: `TaughtIn` (`path`, `section`) is admitted by the engine's own read (`resolveTaughtChildren`, `childNodes(node, "TaughtIn")`, `:1043`) with **0 corpus instances** at HEAD, so it is legal even though the walk sees none; `PaidBy` is layer-conditional (present on all 125 retired `Finding`s in the corpus, optional on live `Finding` because `--stamp-paid-by` writes it there before the move, `:1086`); `Successor` is retired-`Row`-only (3 corpus instances); `CodifiedIn`/`TaughtIn` appear on `Decision` in either layer (8 retired decisions carry 10 `CodifiedIn`). Which children are layer-conditional is asserted by the schema, not inferred from observed presence. The schema is expressed once, in the new helper module `scripts/record-serialize.ts`, and consumed by the engine's shape check. **Measured at HEAD: the proposed schema has 0 violations across all seven files** (206+125 `Finding`, 61+8 `Decision`, 12+62 `Row`, 400 `Entry`), so no data repair is in scope — the schema is a formalization, and the enforcement is what changes. The default validation and all four write modes (`--split`, `--retire`, `--stamp-paid-by`, `--rewrite-roots`) check the schema before any write; a violation refuses the mode (exit non-zero, nothing written) rather than writing a document the serializer cannot canonicalize. This Goal touches no line metric: `F206`'s structural volume metric is explicitly not this bundle's (`NonGoals`).

**The canonical serializer (`F221`), on every write.** Define the record's canonical form: two spaces of indent per depth, a close tag at its open tag's indent, self-closing empty elements, attribute order canonical per element type (root `base` `headroom` `ceiling`; `Finding`/`Decision` `id` `token` `status`; `Row` `name` `status` `kind`; `Entry` `id` `token` `genre` `layer`; `CodifiedIn` `kind`; `TaughtIn` `path` `section`), entity escaping of `&` `<` `>` `"`, a trailing newline after the root close tag, and — the load-bearing half — **body prose preserved exactly**: only structural whitespace is canonicalized; no text node is re-wrapped, reindented or otherwise touched. The serializer lives in `scripts/record-serialize.ts` and every record write routes through it: the 19 textual `writeFileSync` occurrences in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` (one import plus 18 call sites at `:456`, `:557`–`:563`, `:579`, `:1086`, `:1319`–`:1325`, `:1433`) — the import line excluded, all 18 call sites write record artifacts (the inventory at `:456`, the split's seven files and the stub at `:557`–`:579`, `--stamp-paid-by`'s `findings.xml` at `:1086`, `--retire`'s seven files at `:1319`–`:1325`, and `--rewrite-roots`'s up-to-four files at `:1433`). Idempotence is a shipped test: `serialize(parse(serialize(x)))` is byte-equal to `serialize(x)` over the seven golden fixtures and the planted test documents; the durable property over the live files is **canonical at rest** (`AC-CANONICAL-AT-REST`). **The one-time reflow measured at HEAD adds and removes 0 lines per file and changes 0 bytes** across all seven files — every file already satisfies the canonical form (0 top-level gap anomalies, 0 nested-indent anomalies, canonical attribute order, trailing newline present) — so the reflow is a byte no-op and no ceiling is at risk; structural identity across it is proven by the shipped `prove-record-preservation` returning 0 findings plus a parse-equality walk (decoded tree equality before and after); the measurement itself lives in `Assumptions`. **The golden fixtures are regenerated, the population measured (`F265`).** The seven files under `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/` are byte-pinned by `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2147`, and their own bytes are not canonical: golden `rulings.xml` holds 5 of 61 `Decision`s at four-space indent and golden `rulings-retired.xml` holds all 5 at column zero (10 top-level gap anomalies). A serializer on every write therefore changes them, which is `F221`'s own priced one-time cost ("the regeneration of every byte-pinned fixture"); they are regenerated by the fixture builder against the serializer's canonical output, and the shipped golden relation test keeps its title, now asserting the regenerated canonical bytes — the re-capture is the pin this bundle flips. The predicate fixtures under `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/input/` are **not** canonicalized: they are the committed input snapshot the builder materializes verbatim, the engine's canonical output is what the goldens assert, and the input's own 82 top-level gaps (findings 28, findings-retired 33, rulings 5, rulings-retired 5, registry-retired 11) stay on purpose. **Write-path unification, folded here and not deferred:** routing every writer through the serializer exposes the split path's dead copy of the rulings headroom formula (`Math.floor(2 * median(...))` at `:522`) beside the retire path's live one (`Math.floor(7 * median(...))` at `:1273`); the two are replaced by one shared headroom function using the **retire path's constant** (7x, the shipped writer of existing-record ceilings), the split path's copy is removed, and a test asserts both modes derive the same headroom from the same input. A hash identity check is named in `NonGoals` as the successor's.

**The repository-boundary refusal (`F235`).** The engine resolves the repository boundary from the tree — the presence of `.ngrace/` at the cwd, never git (this repository carries the `RM-GITLESS-INTEGRITY` plan, whose `review.md` establishes that a GRACE project need not be a repository; read it before choosing) — and refuses, before any read or write and with a named message, a record directory that resolves outside that boundary. The refusal is the remedy `F235`'s owner names, not the walk-up: the whole-repository copy run from inside the copy is accepted and moves; a partial copy of the record directory alone, passed from the real root, is refused. Both directions are probed on throwaway copies (the whole-repository copy is the `F231` faithful form), and the refusal message names the path, the boundary, and the faithful-copy remedy.

**The separator sweep (`F252`).** One exported normalization (`stripBodySeparator`) removes a trailing separator, defined on the **whitespace-stripped tail** so trailing whitespace cannot hide it: the helper strips trailing whitespace and blank lines from a body's decoded text, then removes a final `---` line and the blank gap before it, and keeps a single trailing newline (so the canonical render puts `</Body>` on its own line). It is applied at the parse boundary (`parseFrozenMarkdown`, so that every rendered `<Body>` is clean and the flush writes clean bytes), in the one-time sweep of the 68 existing bodies (31 live findings, 23 retired findings, 13 live decisions, 1 retired decision), and in the preservation walk, so all three agree on bytes. The three shapes the trim must catch, and the walk's red-direction fixtures, are: a plain `---` as the last line; a `---` followed by a blank line (`rulings.xml`'s `d20`, which the population counts and a raw-last-line helper misses); and the same-line `---</Body>`. The trim removes two lines for the first and third shapes and three for `d20`'s. `record-inventory.json` is the **split's provenance snapshot** — a JSON array of 299 `{token, id, bodyHash}` entries written only by `--split` (`:456`), the record's 400 `Finding`/`Decision` ids minus the 101 entries flushed after the split — not a living manifest; it keeps that role, and the sweep recomputes the 56 hashes it holds for bodies whose separator tail it removes, with a parse-equality proof that only the separator tail moved. The flush leaves the inventory untouched, exactly as every flush since the split has. A flush-invariant walk asserts, over every layer and after the same whitespace strip, that no `<Body>` ends with a separator line. **The sweep touches retired siblings, and that is a permitted write**: searched 2026-09-16, no ruling in `rulings.xml` or `rulings-retired.xml` and no sentence in `docs/plans/README.md` makes a retired body immutable beyond the move; ceilings are live-root-only and are written only by `--retire` (never raised), so a whitespace clean of a retired body neither moves an entry nor touches a ceiling. The sweep's measured line deltas are recorded in `Assumptions`.

**The flush, and the close.** Flush the staged buffer's three entries through the shipped parser and the new serializer — this is the last sanctioned hand flush; the flush/mint verb is the chartered successor — writing `F252` and `F265` live into `findings.xml`, `D40` live into `rulings.xml` with **no `CodifiedIn`** (the `D38` manner, "not yet built"), one index `Entry` per entry in `decisions.xml` (three), the chartered registry row `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2-0785BD5E` into `registry.xml` with `<Pays>F207 F221 F235 F252 F265</Pays>` and a token-free `StatusText` (the inventory is left untouched, exactly as every flush since the split has); then `--rewrite-roots` re-derives all four live roots holding ceilings. The close's `--retire` moves the five findings and the row (`moved 6`), flips the five index layers in place, and leaves `D40` live. Order of operations: serializer lands first; then the separator sweep (bodies and the 56 affected inventory hashes); then the flush; then `--rewrite-roots`; then the close. The flush is performed at the start of execution, under the `D30` window this bundle itself opens.
